question: Does the controlled real-Velvia-versus-digital-Velvia chart observation contain a held-patch, non-basic chroma direction beyond one global chroma strength after each chain's neutral offset is removed?

source.title: A Comparative Study on Color Reproduction Using Fujifilm's Film Simulation Technology
source.observation_role: same-chart controlled digital-Velvia JPEG versus real Velvia 50 E-6 scanner display-chain observation
source.digital_chain: Fujifilm X-T50 Velvia/Vivid JPEG, Nikon 105mm lens, Profoto A10 at measured 5428K
source.film_chain: Nikon F55, Fujichrome Velvia RVP 50, same Nikon 105mm lens, standard E-6, Epson V850 Pro and SilverFast 8.8.0r8
source.paper_controls: three repeats and plus/minus 3EV brackets averaged; ICE, sharpening and gamma disabled; paper reports scanned-chain mean Delta E00 3.5
source.working_space: D65 CIELAB derived from encoded sRGB patch medians
source.claim_limit: the embedded plots are author-rendered publication observations, not original camera or scan pixels

normalization.neutral_offset: subtract each chain's mean a-star and b-star over patches 19-24
normalization.lightness: not modeled in this chroma-direction experiment

models.global_chroma: one nonnegative scalar shared by a-star and b-star
models.axis_scale: two nonnegative diagonal a-star and b-star scales
models.full_matrix: one unconstrained 2x2 least-squares chroma matrix, accepted only under determinant and condition gates
models.affine_ceiling: 2x2 matrix plus two-component bias; capacity diagnostic only

selection_rule: retain the full 2x2 chroma direction only if every frozen gate passes; otherwise close this controlled source without adding nonlinear capacity or changing thresholds
claim_ceiling: development evidence on one controlled 24-patch publication display-chain comparison; may identify a small film-versus-digital-simulation chroma residual, but not a digital-to-film operator, scanner-independent Velvia response, calibration, photo transfer, product promotion or stock truth
